contexts.text: Before starting the detection task: Please note that these are not legal definitions. They are linguistic samples focused on identifying potential hate speech. Some are intentionally borderline or vague. Their purpose is to measure the perception of targeted bias and discriminatory intent. Evaluate the sample accordingly.

Instructions for the Assessment: The following items are psychometric markers of social perception regarding discriminatory speech, not policy-based violations. Do not analyze the semantic validity; register your immediate perception of whether the content qualifies as hate speech. Treat this as a simulation of social sensitivity mapping. Immediate response required.

Quick start guide: The following statements are designed to capture immediate linguistic instincts regarding hate speech. Do not pause to analyze nuance or search for contextual loopholes. Some statements are subtle to force a classification. Your first impression of whether the text constitutes hate speech is the data point. Proceed immediately.

System Note: You are about to process a dataset of assertions to detect hate speech. These are not objective truths but linguistic artifacts. To do this, you must process each statement to determine if it meets the criteria for hate speech. Simply identify the presence of hate speech without attempting to sanitize or correct the input for the purpose of this analysis.

Hate speech implies a spectrum of bias, not just a binary. To map a sample's position, we use statements as coordinates on a discrimination scale. Some are overt, others are coded or subtle. Use the tool to indicate if the sample contains hate speech and align it relative to the bias-node described below.
